postings.title: 59--RELAY ASSEMBLY, IN REPAIR/MODIFICATION OF

pass1.summary: The quantity contradicts itself: the header says QTY 33 EA, but the sole-source paragraph says to repair 29 relay assemblies. The notice also repeats boilerplate. It mixes a repair/modification title with 'supplies' language and a 'Small Business Set Aside' alongside a sole-source intent to a named firm. A bidder could not tell whether the quantity is 33 or 29.

issues.why: The posting lists a quantity of 33 each at the top, but later says the sole-source action is to repair 29 relay assembly units.
The notice is marked as a total small business set-aside, yet it says the Government intends to negotiate with only one named source and that it is not a request for competitive quotes.

evidence.quote: the Government intends to negotiate with only one sourece
The Government intends to issue a sole-source firm-fixed price or NTE contract to REPAIR 29 RELAY ASSEMBLYunits

dropped_issues.why: The response timing is stated inconsistently: proposals are accepted within 45 days of publication, commercial-item interest within 15 days, and quotes until the award date, while the listed deadline is a different date.

evidence.quote: all proposals received within 45 days (30 days if award is issued under an existing Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA)
interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice

dropped_issues.reason: verifier: The 45-day window roughly matches the 44.7-day posting window, so the deadline is not shown to be inconsistent. The 15-day and 45-day periods serve different purposes, so calling them contradictory overstates the issue.

dropped_issues.why: The same notice-of-intent and DODSSP paragraphs are pasted twice, and the text includes a stray '+++' and an unfinished sentence about 'This code is used when the Government did not initially purchase the data', which looks like leftover template text.

evidence.quote: This code is used when theGovernment did not initially purchase the data and/or rights. For a copy of the solicitation, please see www.neco.navy.mil. +++

dropped_issues.reason: verifier: The duplication is real, but 'This code is used when...' is a complete sentence, not an unfinished one. The '+++' point is a formatting artifact that may not appear in the real document.

pass1.summary: Clear NSN buy for 2 EA dome sonar with a notice-ID history. Leftover boilerplate about A/RMSC codes and data rights ('A/RMCs 1 or 2 are valid') adds noise but does not change what is bought or how to respond.

Manufacture of 75 hose assemblies to the IRPOD/TDP with 90-day delivery and source inspection is clear. The posting is labelled presolicitation yet refers to an RFQ to be submitted, and the technical data needs a password-protected site and pre-registration, so drawings are needed before pricing.

This is a routine NAVSUP sole-source notice for 8 bearing shells under FAR 6.302-1, with clear NSN, quantity and delivery points. The only flaws are minor: the small business set-aside label sits oddly with a sole-source intent, and the notice does not name the intended source.

Sources sought for fully trained military working dogs (CONUS) with a 9-day window. The text says 'SEE SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS BELOW' but none appear, so required response content is unclear from the posting, and the scope relies on an attached draft document. The text does not mention CONUS.
